edges.description: Lysosomal storage drives CNS glial activation and neuronal loss.
Undegraded oligosaccharide and glycopeptide substrates spill over into urine.
Somatic glycoprotein storage in craniofacial connective tissues contributes to coarse facial features.
Skeletal storage pathology produces dysostosis multiplex.
Multisystem somatic glycan storage impairs postnatal physical growth.
Storage pathology in auditory neural and middle-ear structures causes sensorineural and mixed hearing loss.
Glycan storage and circulating oligosaccharides impair host mucosal clearance and immune function, predisposing to recurrent infections.
Endothelial lysosomal glycoconjugate storage causes dermal capillary ectasia and angiokeratomas in several glycoproteinoses.
Chronic neuronal dysfunction, synaptic impairment, and neuronal loss underlie progressive intellectual disability.
Microglial activation and neuronal loss produce progressive neurodegeneration.
CNS neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration manifest with seizures.

evidence.reference_title: A 37-Year-Old Man With Intellectual Disability Discovered to Have Aspartylglucosaminuria: Implications for the Diagnosis of Genetic Causes.
evidence.snippet: We identified homozygous donor splice-site variants in the AGA gene (aspartylglucosaminidase; NM_000027.4) Chr4(GRCh38):g. 177436275C>A, c.698+1G>T. This gene is implicated in aspartylglucosaminuria (AGU; OMIM #208400) and originated from both of the patient's parents.

nodes.description: Angiokeratomas (angiokeratoma corporis diffusum) occur in longer-surviving patients across fucosidosis, sialidosis, galactosialidosis, beta-mannosidosis, and Kanzaki disease.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: Angiokeratoma, which is among the symptoms of fucosidosis, is seen in GM1 gangliosidosis, sialidosis type II, Schindler neuroaxonal dystrophy syndrome, Kanzaki disease, galactosialidosis, and β-mannosidosis, but it is not distinctive for Fabry disease.

evidence.reference_title: A New Case of Schindler Disease.
evidence.snippet: Schindler disease type II (also known as Kanzaki disease) is characterised by lymphoedema, angiokeratoma corporis diffusum, neurological involvement, peripheral neuropathy, sensorineural hearing loss and recurrent vertigo attacks (with doubtful association with Ménière’s disease).

nodes.description: Coarse facies are a recurrent somatic feature across the oligosaccharidoses.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: So, fucosidosis is characterized by rapid mental and motor loss, along with growth retardation, coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, telangiectasis or angiokeratomas, epilepsy, inguinal hernia, and dysostosis multiplex.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.
evidence.snippet: The facial trait include large head with prominent forehead, rounded eyebrows, flattened nasal bridge, macroglossia, widely spaced teeth, and prognathism.

nodes.description: Skeletal dysplasia (dysostosis multiplex) accompanies somatic glycoprotein storage across multiple members.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: So, fucosidosis is characterized by rapid mental and motor loss, along with growth retardation, coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, telangiectasis or angiokeratomas, epilepsy, inguinal hernia, and dysostosis multiplex.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Main features are immune deficiency (manifested by recurrent infections, especially in the first decade of life), skeletal abnormalities (mild-to-moderate dysostosis multiplex, scoliosis and deformation of the sternum), hearing impairment (moderate-to-severe sensorineural hearing loss), gradual impairment of mental functions and speech, and often, periods of psychosis.

nodes.description: Intravenous enzyme replacement therapy is approved for non-neurological manifestations of alpha-mannosidosis (velmanase alfa) and under preclinical investigation for other oligosaccharidoses such as fucosidosis and aspartylglucosaminuria; limited blood-brain barrier penetration restricts CNS efficacy.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy and safety of Velmanase alfa in the treatment of patients with alpha-mannosidosis: results from the core and extension phase analysis of a phase III multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
evidence.snippet: These findings support the utility of VA for the treatment of AM, with more evident benefit over time and when treatment is started in the paediatric age.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: In another treatment approach, enzyme replacement therapy, preclinical studies are ongoing for fucosidosis, but the blood-brain barrier is a major obstacle in lysosomal storage diseases affecting the central nervous system.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: Fucosidosis is a rare lysosomal storage disease caused by α-L-fucosidase deficiency following a mutation in the FUCA1 gene

nodes.description: Postnatal growth retardation and abnormal growth trajectories occur across several glycoproteinoses.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: So, fucosidosis is characterized by rapid mental and motor loss, along with growth retardation, coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, telangiectasis or angiokeratomas, epilepsy, inguinal hernia, and dysostosis multiplex.

nodes.description: Sensorineural or mixed hearing impairment is prominent in alpha- and beta-mannosidosis and reported in other oligosaccharidoses.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Main features are immune deficiency (manifested by recurrent infections, especially in the first decade of life), skeletal abnormalities (mild-to-moderate dysostosis multiplex, scoliosis and deformation of the sternum), hearing impairment (moderate-to-severe sensorineural hearing loss), gradual impairment of mental functions and speech, and often, periods of psychosis.

nodes.description: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation supplies donor-derived enzyme-competent cells and can normalize leukocyte enzyme activity and stabilize neurocognitive decline when performed early in selected members (such as alpha-mannosidosis and fucosidosis), whereas it has not proved effective in aspartylglucosaminuria and carries substantial transplant-related morbidity.

evidence.reference_title: Effective treatment of alpha-mannosidosis by allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
evidence.snippet: HCT can halt the progressive cognitive loss in patients with alpha-mannosidosis. Early diagnosis and treatment with HCT is critical for optimal results.

evidence.reference_title: Aspartylglycosaminuria: a review.
evidence.snippet: Allogenic stem cell transplantation has not proved effective in curing AGU.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: So, fucosidosis is characterized by rapid mental and motor loss, along with growth retardation, coarse facial features, hepatosplenomegaly, telangiectasis or angiokeratomas, epilepsy, inguinal hernia, and dysostosis multiplex.

nodes.description: Progressive intellectual disability is a shared neurological feature across the group.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: Chronic neuroinflammation impairs synaptic plasticity and neuronal survival, leading to progressive intellectual disability, learning difficulties, and loss of previously acquired skills.

evidence.reference_title: Aspartylglycosaminuria: a review.
evidence.snippet: Progressive intellectual and physical disability is the main symptom leading to death usually before the age of 50 years.

nodes.description: Deficiency of a lysosomal glycosidase or glycosylasparaginase (e.g., alpha-L-fucosidase, alpha-mannosidase, aspartylglucosaminidase, sialidase) blocks the stepwise lysosomal degradation of N- and O-linked glycans of glycoproteins, glycolipids, and oligosaccharides.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: This enzyme is responsible for breaking down fucose-containing glycoproteins, glycolipids, and oligosaccharides within the lysosome

evidence.reference_title: Aspartylglycosaminuria: a review.
evidence.snippet: The disease is caused by the deficient activity of the lysosomal enzyme glycosylasparaginase (aspartylglucosaminidase, AGA), which leads to a disorder in the degradation of glycoasparagines

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.
evidence.snippet: The disorder is caused by lysosomal alpha-mannosidase deficiency.

nodes.description: Undegraded oligosaccharides and glycopeptides accumulate in lysosomes across visceral, mesenchymal, and neural tissues, engorging the organelle and causing secondary metabolic and cellular dysfunction as well as spillover of undegraded glycans into body fluids and urine.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in FUCA1 result in either reduced enzyme activity or complete loss of function, leading to the accumulation of fucose-rich substrates in lysosomes. Lysosomes become engorged with undigested substrates, which leads to secondary storage defects affecting other metabolic pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Aspartylglycosaminuria: a review.
evidence.snippet: The disease is caused by the deficient activity of the lysosomal enzyme glycosylasparaginase (aspartylglucosaminidase, AGA), which leads to a disorder in the degradation of glycoasparagines - aspartylglucosamine or other glycoconjugates with an aspartylglucosamine moiety at their reducing end - and accumulation of these undegraded glycoasparagines in tissues and body fluids.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Alpha-mannosidosis is inherited in an autosomal recessive fashion and is caused by mutations in the MAN2B1 gene

nodes.description: Progressive neurodegeneration from chronic lysosomal dysfunction and neuroinflammation.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: The central nervous system is particularly vulnerable, with lysosomal dysfunction causing microglial activation, inflammation, and neuronal loss, leading to the neurodegenerative symptoms of fucosidosis.

evidence.reference_title: Mapping Lysosomal Storage Disorders with Neurological Features by Cellular Pathways: Towards Precision Medicine.
evidence.snippet: The neurological system, with its high metabolic demands and vulnerability to impaired clearance mechanisms, is particularly affected, leading to clinical phenotypes ranging from developmental delay to severe neurodegeneration.

nodes.description: CNS lysosomal dysfunction causes microglial activation, neuroinflammation, neuronal apoptosis, axonal degeneration, and synaptic dysfunction, producing the progressive neurodegenerative features of the oligosaccharidoses.

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: The central nervous system is particularly vulnerable, with lysosomal dysfunction causing microglial activation, inflammation, and neuronal loss

evidence.reference_title: Fucosidosis: A Review of a Rare Disease.
evidence.snippet: Neuroinflammation contributes to secondary damage, including neuronal apoptosis, axonal degeneration, and synaptic dysfunction, exacerbating the disease process.

nodes.description: Urinary excretion of undegraded oligosaccharides and glycopeptides is the shared biochemical hallmark and screening abnormality of this disease group.

evidence.reference_title: A 37-Year-Old Man With Intellectual Disability Discovered to Have Aspartylglucosaminuria: Implications for the Diagnosis of Genetic Causes.
evidence.snippet: We confirmed the pathogenicity of the variant by detecting the splicing defect in cDNA from the patient's blood and accumulation of aberrant metabolites in the patient's urine.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.
evidence.snippet: Elevated urinary secretion of mannose-rich oligosaccharides is suggestive, but not diagnostic.

nodes.description: Recurrent respiratory and middle-ear infections occur frequently across fucosidosis, alpha-mannosidosis, and aspartylglucosaminuria.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha-mannosidosis.

evidence.snippet: An infantile growth spurt and development of macrocephalia associated to hernias and respiratory infections are the key signs to an early identification of AGU.
